userStories.title: Inline wiki TOC in system prompt — nanobot MEMORY-in-context pattern
userStories.description:
Nanobot inlines its MEMORY.md into the system prompt every turn (agent/context.py:50-52, cap 32 KB at memory.py:872). For 'what's X' queries where X is in memory, the LLM has the fact INSTANTLY — zero tool calls. Aura's equivalent: inject a compact wiki TOC (slug + 1-line summary per page) into the system prompt so trivial wiki lookups never hit a tool. (a) NEW MODULE internal/wiki/toc.go: GenerateTOC(store *Store, maxBytes int) (string, error). Reads all wiki/*.md, extracts {slug, title, category, tags} from frontmatter + the FIRST non-empty body paragraph (≤120 chars). Renders as: `## Wiki TOC
[[slug]] — Title — first-line-summary
[[slug]] — ...`. (b) BUDGET: default 16 KB cap (half of nanobot's 32 KB since Aura's wiki has fewer but more important pages). When over cap, prefer pages with confidence-labels EXTRACTED + most-recently-updated. (c) CACHED: TOC is rebuilt on wiki write (via wiki.Store post-write hook) and stored in-memory + SQLite (key='wiki:toc', value=blob). System prompt builder reads the cached blob. NO LLM call. (d) PROMPT WIRING in internal/conversation/system_prompt.go: append the TOC after the existing AGENT.md/SOUL.md sections. Mark with delimiters: `--- WIKI TOC START ---
{toc}
--- WIKI TOC END ---`. (e) AGENT.md (runtime + defaults) gain a bullet in 'Memoria e wiki': 'La TOC della wiki è SEMPRE nel system prompt. Se la domanda riguarda una pagina che vedi nella TOC, leggila con file action=read + slug — NON cercarla con search_memory.'. (f) TEST: TestGenerateTOC_StaysWithinBudget, TestGenerateTOC_PicksMostRelevantOnOverflow, TestGenerateTOC_RebuildsOnWikiWrite, TestSystemPrompt_IncludesTOC. (g) PERF: TOC generation must complete in ≤200ms even with 500 pages (regex-only extract, no LLM).

userStories.title: Stream-time tool dispatch — execute tools in parallel with LLM stream (codex killer pattern)
userStories.description: Codex's FuturesOrdered<...> queue (session/turn.rs:1750-1891) receives tool futures the INSTANT each OutputItemDone event arrives over the LLM stream. The stream continues delivering text/reasoning/more tool calls WHILE tool I/O runs in parallel. Aura currently waits for the full LLM round to complete, THEN dispatches tools — this serializes ~50% of the latency budget. THIS IS THE BIGGEST LATENCY WIN of the entire prd. (a) REFACTOR internal/agent/loop.go (or internal/agent/executor.go — grep ExecuteToolCalls): when the LLM client streams output items (tool_use, content, reasoning), the loop SHOULD start the tool execution AS SOON AS the tool_use item is complete in the stream, NOT after the full message ends. (b) PARALLELIZATION: use a worker pool + buffered channel pattern. New helper internal/agent/stream_dispatch.go with StreamDispatcher{maxConcurrent int, tools *registry.Registry}. As tool_use items arrive on the LLM event channel, dispatch.Submit(toolCall) starts the execution. dispatch.Wait() collects results. (c) RESULT ORDERING: results MUST be returned in the order the LLM emitted them (FuturesOrdered semantics) — use a slice indexed by toolCallID + a sync.WaitGroup. (d) SAFETY: respect existing per-tool ToolTimeout. Respect existing PhantomToolGuard (don't dispatch a duplicate of an in-flight call). (e) PARALLEL CAP: configurable AURA_AGENT_PARALLEL_TOOLS (default 4). NO more than N tools dispatched simultaneously. (f) BENCHMARK: include a benchmark test (BenchmarkStreamDispatch_ParallelVsSerial) showing for 3-tool turn: serial ~3×t, parallel ~1.2×t (typical worst-case overlap). (g) BACKPRESSURE: if the LLM stream stalls (timeout), in-flight tools are NOT cancelled — let them finish and capture results for the next turn. (h) NO change to /api/chat response shape — tool order/result semantics identical, just faster.

userStories.notes: GROUND-TRUTH BEFORE EDIT: (1) Read docs/restructure-research/codex-fast-lookup-2026-05-21.md carefully — exact pattern in session/turn.rs:1750-1891 (FuturesOrdered) + tools/parallel.rs:88 (RwLock for read-share). (2) Read internal/agent/loop.go IN FULL — understand the current serial dispatch path. (3) Read internal/llm/client.go (or similar) for the streaming interface — what events arrive (tool_use_delta, tool_use_done, content_done, message_done). (4) Read internal/agent/executor.go for ExecuteToolCalls — what it expects as input and returns. ARCHITECTURE: the StreamDispatcher is a NEW layer between the LLM stream consumer and the tool executor. The loop subscribes to LLM events; on tool_use_done, calls dispatcher.Submit. The dispatcher fans out across maxConcurrent goroutines (semaphore pattern: `sem := make(chan struct{}, maxConcurrent)`). Results land in a per-toolCallID slot. On message_done, the loop calls dispatcher.Wait() which blocks until all submitted tools complete, then returns the ordered results. PHANTOM CORRECTOR HOOK: before Submit, check phantomGuard.ShouldDedupCurrent(toolCall). If dup, set result = '[deduped]' WITHOUT executing. RWLOCK PATTERN (optional v1): tools registered as 'parallel_safe' (read-only by description audit US-DRIFT-05) share a read lock; writers take write lock. v0 ignores this — all tools run with simple semaphore. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: DO NOT change tool implementations. DO NOT change LLM client. DO NOT add new tools. ONLY the dispatch path. THIS IS THE BIGGEST STORY of the prd — write thorough tests. INVARIANT: if maxConcurrent==1, behavior is byte-identical to the current serial path. PERF MEASUREMENT: the benchmark MUST measure actual numbers, not estimates. Use httptest.NewServer with a fake LLM that streams 3 tool_use events 50ms apart, and a fake tool that sleeps 500ms. Serial = 1.5s+overhead, parallel = ~500ms+overhead.
